intuition: Save both the values and the running total of each root-to-node path. When you reach a leaf, keep the path if its total matches the target. Give separate path state to different branches so that exploring one branch cannot change the values saved for another.

Keep a stack entry containing the next node, its prefix path, and the prefix sum. Visiting a node creates a new list with that node appended. Siblings may share their parent prefix, but neither mutates it: each child builds its own extension. Carrying a running sum avoids resumming the same prefix at every descendant.

Negative values rule out a tempting pruning shortcut. A prefix greater than target may later decrease, so exploration must continue until the route ends. Only when both children are absent is the sum compared against target. The approach trades some path-copying space for simple ownership of branch state and avoids recursive-depth problems in skewed trees.
Distinct routes with the same values remain distinct answers.

The copied-prefix design is simple and iterative, but a chain copies lengths 1,2,...,h and can take quadratic time even if it yields one path. A more efficient alternative uses iterative enter/exit events and one shared path: append on entry, pop on exit, and copy only matching leaf paths.

That approach takes O(n+L) time and O(h) additional state, where L counts returned path values. The reference keeps fresh prefixes to make branch ownership explicit; its additional pending copies are bounded by O(h²), separately from O(L) returned output.

steps: For targetSum=22, begin at root 5 with empty prefix and total 0.
The left branch extends through 4 and 11, producing path [5,4,11] and total 20.
Leaf 7 gives total 27 and is rejected; leaf 2 gives total 22, so save [5,4,11,2].
Explore the right branch through 8 and 4. Its leaf 5 gives the second match [5,8,4,5].
The other leaves do not total 22. Return the two saved paths, preserving their complete root-to-leaf order.

concept.question: How can every matching root-to-leaf route keep its own history?
intuition: A yes-or-no search can stop at the first match, but this task needs all matching routes. Sharing one changing path without copying saved answers can corrupt earlier results.
Carry both a path’s values and its total down each branch. At a leaf, save the path if its total matches. Give child branches independent histories so exploration never edits an already saved route.
concept.observation: Save only matching complete root-to-leaf paths, with independent result copies.
approach: Extend the current path and total at each node.
At a matching leaf, save its complete path.
Explore all remaining branches with independent path state.
concept.correctness: Each visited path contains exactly its branch’s root-to-current values, and its sum is their total. Every leaf is visited, so every matching complete route is saved. Independent path storage prevents one branch from changing another branch’s history or an earlier saved answer.

complexity.explanation: The reference copies path histories, so visiting nodes can cost tree height per node. Saved path lengths also contribute output work and memory. Active copied histories can use quadratic memory in tree height.

pitfalls: Do not stop after the first match.
